meta: Parmigianino's Baptism of Christ, painted about 1519 at 16, his earliest surviving work, now in Berlin.
about: Parmigianino painted this Baptism of Christ around 1519, when he was only sixteen, and it is his earliest surviving work. It is usually identified with an anecdote in Vasari's Lives of the Artists, which says that after doing wonderful drawings the boy made a panel of his own invention, Saint John baptizing Christ, so fine that viewers still wondered a child had painted it. The painting is now in the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin.

meta: A shepherd courts a shepherdess under a gnarled tree in Gabriel Huquier's print The Eager Shepherd, about 1730.
about: A shepherd makes advances to a shepherdess seated by a gnarled tree on a bank, and another tree frames the right side. An arabesque frame of garlands, shell-work, hooked scrolls and bat-wing ornament surrounds the scene, and the outer edges are shaded. Gabriel Huquier made the print around 1730.

meta: A monkey snatches grapes from fruit and flowers in Jean-Baptiste Oudry's still life of 1724.
about: A monkey, an animal then known for mischief and lust, snatches a few grapes from a heap of fruit and flowers. Oudry received many commissions from Louis XV, who admired his animal and still life painting, and he often combined the two. The museum says the lush, overripe fruit shows the French Rococo taste for the sensual and recalls the 17th-century Flemish pictures he studied. Such paintings usually decorated dining rooms.

meta: Men, a satyr and putti drink from a big wine barrel under an apple tree entwined with vines, after Andrea Mantegna.
about: Under an apple tree twined with grapevines, six men, a satyr and four putti drink wine from a large barrel once used for crushing grapes. A distracted putto looks away. One man sits on another's shoulders and passes a laurel wreath to a third, who also holds a horn of plenty. A satyr in the background drinks from a jug, and a man leaning on the barrel sings in the ear of another swooning over its edge. Two putti sleep below while a third tries to climb in. The print is credited to Andrea Mantegna.

meta: Christ mocked and Christ washing the disciples' feet, with an execution of Queen Mary on the back, by Jan van der Straet, about 1580.
about: On the front left, figures crowd a dark arched space lit by a large candle, with Christ seated at the center, head bowed and hands tied. On the front right, Christ kneels in a dramatically lit interior to wash the feet of his disciples. The back shows Queen Mary lying face down on a square platform with her neck on an execution block, a man tying her hands and the executioner raising an axe. Jan van der Straet made the sheet.

meta: Henry Ossawa Tanner's study for Moses and the Burning Bush, after his trip to the Sinai mountains.
about: Henry Ossawa Tanner drew on the Gospels and on his upbringing in the African Methodist Episcopal Church for his art. Some works, like this study for Moses and the Burning Bush, came from the Hebrew Bible. In the painting an angel of God, in the form of a burning bush, calls on Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. On his second trip to the Middle East Tanner visited the mountains of the Sinai Peninsula, where the episode took place.

meta: The library at Cassiobury Park after James Wyatt's redecoration, sketched by Augustus Charles Pugin, about 1810.
about: This sketch shows the late 17th-century library at Cassiobury Park after James Wyatt redecorated it around 1800. The huge room measured fifty-four by twenty-three feet. Family portraits hang on the walls, along with works by Reynolds, Rubens, Van Dyck, Lely and Kneller, and the carved frame of the Reynolds is by Grinling Gibbons. Three arched windows with swagged curtains are separated by pier mirrors, and a central lantern lights the room. Augustus Charles Pugin made the drawing.

meta: The Nativity, a predella panel by Perugino from 1500 to 1505, one of five scenes of Christ's divinity revealed.
about: This panel is one of four that, with a fifth showing the Resurrection in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, once made up a predella, the row of small pictures at the base of an altarpiece. The scenes show moments when Christ's divine nature was revealed, at his birth, his baptism, his conversation at a well with a Samaritan woman, his resurrection and his appearance to Mary Magdalene. This one is the Nativity, by Perugino. The painting that crowned the altarpiece has not been identified.

meta: Designs for two brooches with strapwork, harpies and masks, plate 13 of René Boyvin's Livre de bijouterie, about 1570.
about: This plate gives designs for two brooches. At the left, strapwork and trophies surround a figure scene, with a mask above. At the right, a strapwork oval with harpies and masks, and fruit, surrounds a central scene with figures and a cow. René Boyvin made plate 13 of his Livre de bijouterie, a book of designs for goldsmiths and jewelers, around 1570.

meta: A Vienna salon with a blue and red carpet, bentwood chairs and japanned cabinets, drawn by Franz Alt, about 1870.
about: An ogee-patterned carpet in blue and red dominates this salon in Vienna. Blue spoon-back chairs are covered in blue velvet with red and blue fringe, and black and gold japanned cabinets and black-family porcelain vases decorate the room. A white and gold Rococo console and a gilt mirror with candelabra stand between the windows. The chandelier in the Louis XV style may have come from Baccarat, and Thonet bentwood chairs with cane seats stand casually about. Franz Alt made the view.

meta: A bearded nobleman in Turkish dress holds a staff topped with a crescent, plate 17 of Joseph Marie Vien's The Sultan's Caravan, about 1740.
about: A bearded man in Turkish costume stands on a porch with a railing and a landscape beyond, facing slightly left. His right hand rests on his hip, and in his left he holds a staff topped with a crescent moon. A crescent and feathers decorate his tall stiff hat, and loops of pearl form his belt. This is plate 17 from The Sultan's Caravan, by Joseph Marie Vien.

meta: Saint Anthony reads his Bible among fantastic demons in Roelandt Savery's landscape of 1617, a celebration of nature.
about: Roelandt Savery turns the temptation of Saint Anthony into a celebration of nature's grandeur. The hermit Anthony sits in a rustic shelter reading a Bible, oblivious to the antics of many fantastic demons around him. Savery was a Flemish painter of landscape and still life. He painted this panel in 1617, and it is in the Getty.

meta: Paneling design for an office with a rococo settee, a candelabrum and a clock topped by Father Time, by François de Cuvilliés, about 1690.
about: At the center of this design is a settee in the Rococo manner, flanked by side tables. The left table holds a candelabrum, and the right one a clock topped with Father Time holding an hourglass and a scythe. The left and right panels are lettered A and B, and a mirror framed with C-curves hangs at the center. The design is by François de Cuvilliés the Elder.
